seen_animation: A line-drawn hat (domed crown, a band drawn as two crossing lines, a flat oval brim) sits level near the top-left-centre in frames 1-4 of a.png. In frame 5 it has moved right and begun to tilt, the brim sloping down to the right and its right end cut by the frame edge. Through frames 6-12 it tilts further and stays on the right side at about the same size, a little smaller in frames 9-10. In frames 13-16 it grows larger, the crown runs off the top of the frame, and the brim slopes steeply down to the right. No scenery is drawn.
seen_film: A man in a white bucket hat and blue hooded sweatshirt sits slumped beside an aluminium chair frame. In frames 1-4 of d.png the hat is level, upper centre, and he looks down and to the left. From frames 5-8 he leans his head down and right and the camera shifts so the hat sits at the upper right, tilting with brim lower on the right. In frames 9-12 he hunches over his folded arm, fiddling with a strap or glasses; the hat stays tilted at upper right. In frames 13-16 the framing tightens, the hat gets larger and crops at the right and top edges, and he fiddles with a drawstring in his hand.
named_subject: A brimmed hat (the white bucket hat worn by the man in the film), drawn as a domed crown with a band and an oval brim.
evidence: The path matches the film overall: level hat in e.png 1-8 (film 1-8 hat level, upper centre), moved right and tilted in 9-24 (film 9-24 hat tilted at upper right), large and cropped at top in 26-32 (film 26-32 hat large and cropped). Judged from still frames only. But the change happens in three steps instead of continuously: e.png 8->9 the hat goes from level and wide to tilted and shifted right in one frame, while film 8->9 shows only a small head movement; 16->17 the whole drawing shrinks by roughly 15 percent in one frame while film 16->17 keeps the hat the same size; 25->26 the crown jumps from fully visible to cut off at the top and the brim lengthens sharply, a larger size step than film 25->26. Within each block (1-8, 9-16, 17-24, 26-32) the drawing barely changes, so it holds still while the film's head keeps drifting and tilting. g.png shows the drawing positions clustered in a few groups rather than an even path.
primary_gap: Tilt, position and scale change in jumps at frames 9, 17 and 26 and hold nearly still in between, instead of changing a little on every frame as the man's head does in the film.
closes_when: Between consecutive e.png frames the brim angle, position and size change by small even amounts, so 8->9, 16->17 and 25->26 show no larger step than any other pair, and frames 2-8 and 18-24 show the gradual drift the film has.
protect: The hat drawing itself matches c.png closely (lumpy domed crown, band as two crossing strokes that overshoot at both ends, wide rounded brim, thin single-weight polyline strokes); the overall sequence of level -> tilted right -> enlarged and cropped matches the film's framing at the right moments; brim slope direction matches the film.
identity_gap: None of consequence: the crown, crossing band strokes and oval brim are the doodle's own construction, only rotated and scaled.
